Subject: Hosted API vs Dedicated — recap & next steps

Hi Jason / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Key requirements I heard:
  • 30k TPS spikes during payroll cut windows (short bursts, ~5–10 mins)
  • P95 latency target <= 200ms for user-facing prompts
  • Data residency in us-east and audit logs retained 12 months
  • Budget sensitivity — want guidance on unit cost at expected volume

- Recommendation (preliminary): Hosted API will give fastest time-to-value for initial launch and easy autoscaling for burst traffic, but for sustained high throughput with predictable unit economics and isolation we should evaluate Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools). Dedicated also helps with tighter tail-latency control under steady state.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm expected steady-state QPS and burst characteristics (avg QPS, peak burst TPS, burst duration)?
2) We'll run a quick latency/throughput simulation for both Hosted and Dedicated using your expected traffic profile — target deliverable by EOD Mon (6/14).
3) I'll attach a short comparison doc and a draft quote to start a procurement conversation if you want to proceed.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-ps.pdf (1 page comparison)

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput sim and ballpark economics (deliverable)

Jason / Priya —

Attached is the short sim I promised plus a ballpark quote: FP-MPA-draft-quote.pdf and redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-ps.pdf. Summary highlights below: 

- Latency (P95) estimates based on your profile (1,200 QPS steady, 30k TPS bursts, 6–8 min):
  • Hosted API: P95 steady = ~90–110ms; burst tail (30k TPS) P95 = ~350–500ms depending on concurrent users and queueing during the burst. Hosted autoscaling helps but short intense bursts will see higher tail latency.
  • Dedicated: P95 steady = ~60–80ms; burst tail (with reserved capacity sized to cover ~70% of expected burst) = ~120–180ms. To cover full 30k TPS bursts without noticeable tail increases we'd recommend a Dedicated cluster with burst pool + autoscale (cost note below).

- Cost (very rough, monthly) assuming your usage pattern (tokens/month estimated in attachment):
  • Hosted API: ~$0.12 per 1k tokens (example) — easier ops, cost varies with volume and caching.
  • Dedicated: Effective unit cost can be ~30–50% lower at your scale depending on commit level and quantization profiles; predictable monthly commitment required.

Recommendation: For initial rollout (MVP), start on Hosted API to validate feature and UX quickly. If you expect to run payroll workloads at scale in production with tight tail-latency SLAs, plan a Dedicated engagement with a reserved capacity contract and a short pilot (1–3 months) to validate tail latency under real traffic.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want, Marissa can prepare a Dedicated sizing + MPA (master purchase agreement) sketch and a more detailed cost model for procurement.
2) We can schedule a 60-min architecture session where our infra team (Dylan) walks through autoscale + burst pool design.

Attachments: FP-MPA-draft-quote.pdf, redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-ps.pdf

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
